text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy summons Egyptian envoy to protest Cairo's anti-Israel attacks.
- Israeli army, South Lebanon Army on alert as Lebanon remains tense.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu leaves for three-day European tour; aide terms them a series of courtesy calls.
- Middle East development bank unlikely as U.S. Congress refuses funding.
HAARETZ
- Deputy Egyptian Foreign Minister: "Netanyahu needs a psychiatrist"; Israel to submit protest.
- Germany demands Israel reduce its requests for equipment in war on terror. Netanyahu, in Bonn, will support Germany's acceptance into U.N. Security Council.
- Prime minister worried United States when he gave a mistaken picture of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's nuclear capabilities.
- Russia will decide soon whether to sell Israel Aircraft Industries transport plane that IAI would sell China as part of a quarter-billion-dollar deal to make a spy plane.
- Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor going to the United States for annual meeting of International Monetary Fund.
- Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel expected to announce lowering of interest rate by 0.5 to 0.8 percentage points.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH

- Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan puts off visit to Israel because of political stalemate. He was supposed to visit on October 6. Political sources: Jordan fears being seen as the only Arab country in close contact with Israel.
- Saudi television: Syria issues 100,000 reserve notices. Sources in Jerusalem: Nothing to this story.
- Egypt: Unprecedented attacks against Netanyahu.
- Islamic Hamas movement issues orders for attacks from prison.
MAARIV
- "Grave worry" in Jerusalem following Egyptian statements against Netanyahu.
- Israeli astronaut to be chosen from five battle pilots.
- Netanyahu's use of English expression "to cut off your nose to spite your face" viewed as an insult to Egypt.
- New one-shekel, two-shekel and 20-shekel coins to be issued at start of December to memory of slain Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin.
